statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk sits in the low band at 13% while stress stays elevated at 54% on crude, a live Fed-hike debate and broad semiconductor weakness.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with a range-respecting regime for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The in-line jobless-claims print has passed without disturbing the overnight band, so the narrow evidence-based danger window has been tightened to 13:30Z-15:00Z, covering the cash open and the ISM Services release. Conditional tail touches the watch band only in the 14:00Z hour and stays below the block threshold for every other hour of the forecast, including the pre-payrolls build at the end of the horizon.
headline: In-line claims leave the Nasdaq-100 inside its overnight band; tail low, stress elevated on crude and rate-hike odds
body: NQ futures trade near 29,117, down about 0.24% against a 29,186.25 previous close, inside a 29,075-29,292.75 overnight band roughly 0.75% wide. Price rotated from the 29,292.75 high back through the previous close, recovered to mid-range and has since eased toward the lower half without testing the 29,075 low, so meaningful mean reversion is present and no session extreme is being defended. Two independent quote sources agree on level, direction and day range. Initial jobless claims for the week ending 29 August printed 206k against 205k consensus, an in-line result that removed a checkpoint cleanly, and the July trade balance was released alongside it. VIX is 15.37, up about 1.1% but low in absolute terms. Long-end yields continue to pull back from three-year highs, with the 10Y at 4.77%, the 2Y at 4.37% and the 30Y at 5.24%, and Treasury futures confirm the bid. The standing macro tension is the live September FOMC debate, where hawkish Jackson Hole commentary has pushed priced hike odds above 50%. Energy remains the clearest amplifier: WTI is 92.05 dollars, up about 1.2% after a 9% three-session run, and Brent is 96.24 dollars, though crude steadied after remarks that renewed strikes would be short-lived. Cross-asset structure is dispersed rather than aligned: Dow futures are firmer while Nasdaq futures are softer, semiconductors are lower across the board with Broadcom down about 3% despite record revenue and AI revenue up 221%, and megacap direction is split. That dispersion supports an elevated stress reading while leaving tail in the low band. Remaining catalysts are the 13:30Z cash open, the 13:45Z S&P Global services final and the 14:00Z ISM Services release, ahead of Friday's August payrolls. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was 48 minutes old and complete at assessment time and was used as supporting confirmation only.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours began in the second half of Wednesday's US session, when the regime was mixed and both scores were decaying from the European-session downdraft that had pushed tail to 20% and stress to 72% on three-year-high long-end yields. Tail fell steadily from 18% to 11% and stress from 68% to 54% through Wednesday afternoon and evening. The Asian and European hours of 3 September have been a flat normal regime with tail confined to 12-14% and stress oscillating between 52% and 57% as crude firmed and eased. Five hourly slots have no published assessment and are marked unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours hold one remaining catalyst cluster and then a long decay into Friday's payrolls. Conditional tail steps from 13% through the 13:00Z cash-open hour, peaks at 21% in the 14:00Z hour where ISM Services overlaps the first half hour of cash trade, then falls back into the low band from 15:00Z as the impulse is assumed to fade. The 19:00Z power hour is a secondary bump. Overnight hours hold 10-11% with unscheduled Middle East headlines as the residual amplifier, before a gradual pre-payrolls build through the European morning that reaches 18% in the final slot ahead of the 12:30Z employment block. Every forecast hour except 14:00Z maps to EA_ON; that single hour maps to WATCH. Forecast confidence decays with horizon by design.
